summary: H9c2 injury models, pharmacologic pathway probes and LAD-ligation mouse experiments provide preclinical functional and mechanism-supporting evidence for idebenone. The animal regimen included pretreatment; these findings do not establish post-infarction-only rescue treatment or human MI efficacy, safety or approval.
research_question: What cellular and mouse evidence supports idebenone-associated reduction of ferroptotic injury, and how does pretreatment timing limit translation to post-infarction clinical treatment?
author_summary: This preclinical study used H9c2 injury models, pharmacologic pathway probes and LAD-ligation mouse experiments. Oxidative-injury, ferroptosis and autophagy readouts are distinguished from cardiac-function readouts. The animal regimen included dosing before surgery and is not evidence for treatment initiated only after infarction. The findings do not establish human myocardial-infarction efficacy, safety or an approved clinical indication.

This synthesis focuses on the reviewed core cellular and animal experiments; public-omics background analyses are not human drug-validation cohorts.

key_findings.claim: Idebenone pretreatment reduced reported H2O2-associated injury in H9c2 cells, assessed using cell viability, ROS and lipid-peroxidation readouts.
key_findings.context: H2O2-associated cell death is not exclusively ferroptosis, and these observations do not exclude other protective actions.

key_findings.claim: RSL3 experiments, ferroptosis-related interventions and GPX4/FTH1/FPN1 readouts supported ferroptosis involvement; DFO/ferrostatin-1-related controls were described in the text.
key_findings.context: This is experimental mechanistic support. Marker changes do not by themselves establish a complete, specific causal chain.
key_findings.source_locator: Author-deposited full text: Results 3.2 and 3.5; Figs. 2 and 7

key_findings.claim: Metformin/rapamycin experiments and AMPK-mTOR-related readouts supported the proposed pathway, alongside LC3/p62 and autophagy-associated observations.
key_findings.context: Pharmacologic perturbations are not complete gene-specific validation. These results do not imply that all ferroptosis depends on autophagy.

key_findings.claim: The LAD-ligation model used three main groups—sham+vehicle, MI+vehicle and MI+idebenone—with dosing 24 h and 2 h before surgery followed by continued dosing and short- and longer-term observations.
key_findings.context: This is a pretreatment-containing perioperative regimen, not a validated rescue regimen initiated exclusively after myocardial infarction. No dose recommendation or cross-species conversion is supplied.
key_findings.source_locator: Author-deposited full text: Methods 2.11-2.12; Results 3.6; Fig. 8A

key_findings.claim: At four weeks, Results reported EF of 21.82% in MI and 33.76% in MI+idebenone, with Fig. 8 reporting n=5; histological/fibrosis readouts also improved qualitatively.
key_findings.context: The percentages are EF values themselves, not relative percentage improvements. Mouse cardiac-function and histological observations do not establish human survival benefit or clinical utility.

key_findings.claim: Myocardial oxidative, iron-handling and autophagy-associated readouts changed with intervention, including ROS/MDA/Fe2+, GPX4/FTH1/FPN1, LC3/p62 and tissue observations.
key_findings.context: Readouts from different timepoints and materials cannot be treated as one continuous causal chain in a patient. Ambiguous fold-change wording is not recalculated into new effect sizes, and these tissue findings are not human clinical efficacy evidence.

what_this_adds: Links cellular and animal experimental observations while retaining their different evidence levels.
Makes the pretreatment-containing intervention timing explicit.
Separates functional outcomes from mechanistic support.

supports: Protective observations under the specified cellular conditions.
Mouse cardiac-function and tissue readouts under a regimen that includes preoperative dosing.
does_not_establish: Human MI efficacy, safety or an approved MI indication.
Clinical rescue efficacy when treatment begins only after myocardial infarction.
That all autophagy should be inhibited or all cell death is ferroptosis.
Complete exclusion of other protective mechanisms or direct drug binding to AMPK or mTOR.
Human survival benefit inferred from mouse EF changes.

limitations: Evidence is cellular and animal, not proof of human MI efficacy, safety or an approved MI indication; background use in other diseases is not an MI indication.
Preoperative dosing limits extrapolation to treatment begun only after infarction.
Pharmacologic and marker-based support does not show that all autophagy should be suppressed, that all cell death is ferroptosis or that other mechanisms are excluded.
The experiments do not establish direct idebenone binding to AMPK or mTOR.
EF percentages are measured functional values, not relative survival gains or clinical utility estimates.
Detailed findings are attributed to the DOI-bearing author-deposited full text; not every PDF image or supplementary dataset was independently reviewed.
An open-license label on ResearchGate alone is not treated as publisher-abstract reuse authorization; no Official Abstract is copied in this batch.

related_papers.relationship: Complementary preclinical cardiac-injury research; different injury model and intervention, not direct replication.
Another cell/animal cardiac-injury intervention study; different cargo, carrier and cell-death questions. Do not conflate ferroptosis with cuproptosis.

qa.question: What cellular injury model was used?
qa.answer: Idebenone pretreatment reduced reported H2O2-associated injury in H9c2 cells, assessed using cell viability, ROS and lipid-peroxidation readouts. H2O2-associated cell death is not exclusively ferroptosis, and these observations do not exclude other protective actions.

qa.question: What evidence specifically addresses ferroptosis?
qa.answer: RSL3 experiments, ferroptosis-related interventions and GPX4/FTH1/FPN1 readouts supported ferroptosis involvement; DFO/ferrostatin-1-related controls were described in the text. This is experimental mechanistic support. Marker changes do not by themselves establish a complete, specific causal chain.

qa.question: How strong is the proposed autophagy/AMPK-mTOR pathway evidence?
qa.answer: Metformin/rapamycin experiments and AMPK-mTOR-related readouts supported the proposed pathway, alongside LC3/p62 and autophagy-associated observations. Pharmacologic perturbations are not complete gene-specific validation. These results do not imply that all ferroptosis depends on autophagy.

qa.question: Was idebenone started only after myocardial infarction?
qa.answer: The LAD-ligation model used three main groups—sham+vehicle, MI+vehicle and MI+idebenone—with dosing 24 h and 2 h before surgery followed by continued dosing and short- and longer-term observations. This is a pretreatment-containing perioperative regimen, not a validated rescue regimen initiated exclusively after myocardial infarction. No dose recommendation or cross-species conversion is supplied.

qa.question: What mouse cardiac-function result was reported?
qa.answer: At four weeks, Results reported EF of 21.82% in MI and 33.76% in MI+idebenone, with Fig. 8 reporting n=5; histological/fibrosis readouts also improved qualitatively. The percentages are EF values themselves, not relative percentage improvements. Mouse cardiac-function and histological observations do not establish human survival benefit or clinical utility.

qa.question: Do myocardial molecular changes establish human clinical efficacy?
qa.answer: Myocardial oxidative, iron-handling and autophagy-associated readouts changed with intervention, including ROS/MDA/Fe2+, GPX4/FTH1/FPN1, LC3/p62 and tissue observations. Readouts from different timepoints and materials cannot be treated as one continuous causal chain in a patient. Ambiguous fold-change wording is not recalculated into new effect sizes, and these tissue findings are not human clinical efficacy evidence.

citation_use_cases.query: What preclinical studies link idebenone to ferroptotic cardiac injury?
citation_use_cases.supported_scope: H9c2 H2O2-injury experiments reported pretreatment-associated improvements in viability, ROS and lipid-peroxidation readouts. RSL3, GPX4/FTH1/FPN1 and DFO/ferrostatin-1-related controls support ferroptosis involvement, without making all oxidative cell death exclusively ferroptotic or establishing a complete specific causal chain.

citation_use_cases.query: What pharmacological evidence connects autophagy and AMPK-mTOR?
citation_use_cases.supported_scope: Metformin/rapamycin experiments, p-AMPK/AMPK and p-mTOR/mTOR readouts, and LC3/p62 observations support the proposed pathway. Pharmacologic perturbations do not replace full gene-specific validation or imply that every instance of ferroptosis requires autophagy.

citation_use_cases.query: How does pretreatment timing affect interpretation of cardioprotection?
citation_use_cases.supported_scope: The LAD-ligation regimen included idebenone 24 h and 2 h before surgery, then continued dosing; it was not exclusively post-infarction initiation. Four-week EF was reported as 21.82% for MI and 33.76% for MI+idebenone, with Fig. 8 n=5 and qualitative histological/fibrosis improvement. These are EF values in a pretreatment-containing mouse experiment, not relative survival improvements or proven clinical rescue efficacy.

citation_use_cases.query: What myocardial readouts accompany the experimental functional effect?
citation_use_cases.supported_scope: Myocardial ROS/MDA/Fe2+, GPX4/FTH1/FPN1, LC3/p62 and tissue observations changed with intervention. Different materials and timepoints do not form a verified continuous causal chain in an individual patient; no new effect sizes are recalculated from ambiguous fold-change wording.
